definition: A long flared dress that fits snugly to the waist then flows to the floor, worn for festive occasions and weddings.
A wrap-front top or dress where one panel of fabric crosses over the other and ties at the side.
A three-piece outfit of a flared skirt, a fitted blouse and a long scarf, worn at Indian weddings and celebrations.
A long flowing scarf draped over the shoulders, across the chest or over the head with a matching tunic set.
A long formal men's coat from North India worn buttoned over trousers at weddings and receptions.
An unstitched length of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs by men for ceremonies, temple visits and daily wear.
A cloth wrapped around the waist and worn by men in South and East India, mainly at home and for daily wear.
A long loose gown from Kashmir worn over other layers to keep out the cold.
A two-piece draped outfit from Assam made of a wrapped lower cloth and a separate shoulder cloth in Assamese weaving.
A half-saree outfit of skirt, blouse and shoulder cloth worn by young girls in South India.
A knee-length tunic worn over loose trousers gathered at the ankle, with a matching scarf, common in Punjab and Kashmir.
A white or cream ankle-length robe worn by men in the African Great Lakes region, often with a jacket and small cap.
A skirt of blackened cowhide worn by married women in southern Africa, given by the bride's father after a coming-of-age ceremony.
A loose-fitting casual shirt with a bold printed pattern, usually worn untucked from the trousers and without a necktie.
A printed wrapper cloth worn by women in the African Great Lakes region around the body or waist.
A floor-length dress with square puffed shoulders and a sash, worn by women in Uganda for formal occasions.
A three-piece robe worn by men in West Africa and parts of the Maghreb on formal occasions.
A cloak worn over a robe by tribal chiefs, imams and kings at formal events.
A sleeveless denim or leather vest covered in patches and metal studs showing music taste or political views, worn in punk circles.
Tight trousers fitted with straps, metal fastenings and sometimes a rear flap, worn in punk style.
A laced and boned bodice that covers the chest and shapes the whole torso, worn in Victorian-style goth outfits.
A loose sleeveless outer wrap with a hood, worn for dramatic volume and movement in goth dress.
A sleeveless dress with shoulder straps worn over a blouse, central to Lolita fashion.
A suspender-style dress or skirt held up by straps, more casual and playful than a formal jumperskirt.
An underskirt worn beneath a dress or skirt to give it volume and a bell or A-line shape.
Short gathered undershorts worn beneath a skirt for comfort, coverage or old-fashioned styling.
A jacket of woven fabric bonded to a fleece back, wind-resistant and breathable but not waterproof, used as the daily outer layer.
Tapered trousers with bent knees, a gusseted crotch and cargo pockets placed so they do not interfere when seated.
Waterproof shell trousers with full-length side zips so they pull on over boots, worn in wet weather.
A soft brushed-cotton shirt with a buttoned front, worn in skate-punk style for comfort and practicality.
A wooden-soled thong sandal with two raised wooden blocks beneath, worn with kimono to keep feet and hems above wet ground.
A low-cut leather slipper from northern India with a curled toe and heavy embroidery, covering only the heel and toes.
A slipper made from one piece of soft deerskin with a flexible sole and beaded or embroidered upper, from Native North America.
Basket-like shoes woven from linden or birch bark fibres, cheap and quick to make but not durable, from northern Europe.
A clog carved from a single piece of wood that protects the foot from mud and falling objects, from the Netherlands.
A South African walking shoe with a vegetable-tanned leather or rawhide upper stitched to the footbed without nails or tacks.
A Japanese sandal woven from rice straw and tied to the foot and ankle with cords.
A Japanese split-toe work boot with a rubber sole, worn by construction workers and tradespeople.
A Vietnamese sandal cut from old vehicle tyre rubber, held on the foot by rubber straps.
A shoe or boot with a long sharply pointed toe, popular in British youth and goth styles.
A cone-shaped straw hat worn in East and Southeast Asia to shade the head from sun and rain.
A traditional Korean men's hat with a cylindrical crown and wide brim, made of horsehair and bamboo.
A tall lambskin fur hat traditional in Bulgaria, Turkey, Ukraine and Central Asia, made in regional styles.
A straw hat made in Chile, worn by rural horsemen for shade.
A bamboo hat with a conical top worn by farmers in Bangladesh to shield them from sun and rain.
A tall pleated brimless cylindrical hat worn by chefs to cover the hair and repel sweat in the kitchen.
A handwoven basket-style bag of vegetable twine with leather trimmings, from the Taita, Kikuyu and Kamba peoples of Kenya.
A structured leather bag with a wide hinged-frame opening, top handle and secure clasp, based on the case carried by physicians.
A structured rounded rectangular bag with top handles, originally made to carry a bowling ball.
A flat bag whose closing flap is shaped like an envelope, carried for formal events and evenings out.
A small narrow rectangular bag with a short strap carried tucked under the arm, closed by a zipper or snap.
A structured bag with a metal frame around its opening and a clasp closure.
A large flat folding bag with handles that carries suits or dresses on trips without creasing them.
A small pouch on an adjustable strap worn around the waist so the hands stay free.
A roomy bag with many pockets for carrying a baby's diapers, wipes, bottles and spare outfits.
A small pouch with a clasp or zipper that holds loose coins and a few small items.
A pendant hung from a chain at the hair parting so it rests on the forehead, worn by Indian brides.
A bell-shaped earring with pearls or enamel work, worn with festive and bridal outfits in India.
A large nose ring worn by brides, spiralled in Maharashtra or hooped in Punjab and Rajasthan, sometimes chained to the ear.
A necklace of black beads and gold worn by Hindu married women as a sign of marriage.
A hand ornament joining a bracelet to finger rings with fine chains, worn by Indian brides and dancers.
A silver ring worn on the toes by married women in North and South India.
A silver ankle chain, often hung with small bells that chime when the wearer walks.
A finger ring carrying an engraved seal or emblem, once pressed into wax to mark documents.
A pair of small fasteners that pass through buttonholes to close the cuffs of a shirt.
A safety pin pushed through the skin and worn as a body piercing in early punk style.
A thin plain wristwatch with a slim case and flat crystal built to slide under a shirt cuff.
A small wristwatch with high-contrast markers, a low crystal and a fabric or leather strap, descended from military issue.
A wristwatch with a rotating bezel used to time an interval underwater, with strong water resistance.
Eyeglasses with no earpieces whose lenses are held on by pinching the bridge of the nose.
Tinted lenses in thin metal frames that grew out of sun lenses made for army pilots.
A thin curved lens placed directly on the eye to correct vision and replaced after a set period.
A smooth flat stone pressed and dragged along the face and neck to massage the skin.
A handheld roller with a chilled head rolled over the face to cool and tighten the skin.
A handheld roller with a rose quartz stone head pressed over the face to massage in skincare products.
A soft silicone-bristled brush used to scrub dirt, oil and makeup from the face.
A hinged metal cutter squeezed to trim fingernails and toenails, often with a small file attached.
An electric cutter with a row of fast-moving blades and clip-on guards for choosing hair length, used for fades and buzz cuts.
A small light cutter with fine blades used to shape hairlines, ears and beard edges with clean lines.
A comb with fine teeth on one side and wide teeth on the other for detangling and styling hair.
A razor holding a single or double-sided replaceable blade, giving a close shave for sensitive or ingrown-prone skin.
A hair arrangement shaved at the sides and stiffened into a central ridge or tall spikes, dyed in bright colours.
A disc of compressed tea leaves weighing 200 to 357 grams, kept and aged for later brewing.
A small compressed lump of pu-erh tea leaves sold by weight and stored for later brewing.
A slide-lid or hinged wooden box holding 25 or 50 cigars loose, used to sell and store them.
One rolled-tobacco cigar, for example a 5 by 50 robusto, lit and smoked over about an hour.
A concentrated alcohol-free perfume oil distilled onto a sandalwood or oud base, dabbed on pulse points with a glass rod.
A bottle of perfume holding 15 to 20 percent fragrance oil, sprayed on skin and lasting six to ten hours.
A bottle of Chinese sorghum spirit rested in terracotta jars, collected in decorative packaging when old or rare.
A bottle of Scotch whisky from Islay, made from barley dried over peat fires and prized for its smoky taste.
A sleeveless fluorescent vest with reflective bands worn by roadside and warehouse workers so vehicles can see them.
A hard shell worn on the head against falling objects and bumps on building sites, with a chin strap.
Close-sealing eye covers worn against dust, liquid splashes and flying particles in labs and workshops.
A one-piece work suit of treated fabric worn where sparks or flame threaten the wearer.
A work boot with a reinforced metal toe cap that protects the foot from heavy falling objects.
A flat square cap with a tassel on a centre button, worn with academic gowns at graduation.
A broad-brimmed felt hat with the brim folded up and pinned front and back, worn by European officers around 1790.
A robe and wig worn by judges and lawyers in the law courts of Commonwealth countries.
Spectacles with built-in screens and cameras that show information or capture images in front of the wearer's eyes.
A strapped-on visor with screens and lenses that fills the wearer's view with a virtual scene.
A sealed box lined with cedar that holds cigars at a steady humidity.
A handle with a roller studded with fine needles rolled over the skin to stimulate collagen.
Strings of glass, wood or metal beads worn around the hips, marking womanhood, beauty and status in West African cultures.
A loop of knotted or strung beads counted through the fingers while reciting prayers, such as a rosary or japa mala.
A wrist band engraved with a wearer's health condition so responders can read it in an emergency.
A pair of stamped metal identification plates on a chain worn by soldiers.
A finger ring made of interlocking bands that fall apart and must be solved to put back together.
A folding canopy on a handle held over the head to keep off rain or sun.
A rugged multi-pocket bag for carrying hand tools to a job site.
A strapped harness worn with a lanyard to catch a worker who falls from height.
